brief: TS Lombard expects the Fed to lean hawkish at the October FOMC meeting given strengthening US macro data. The firm argues the roughly 30bp pullback in 10y yields since early October reflects markets pricing a higher chance of an AI-bust scenario that could force aggressive Fed cuts; if that fear fades, yields face renewed upside because jobless claims are at 57-year lows, growth is solid (Atlanta Fed Nowcast running 4.3% for Q3), inflation surprised higher again, and price pressures (oil, ISM prices paid, shipping, food, inflation expectations, Fed speak) are not abating. Kevin Warsh wants inflation back to target quickly, making the Fed less likely to wait for disinflation given higher second-round-effect risk in the US. TS Lombard says this hawkish backdrop could drive the next leg lower in homebuilders, whose margins are already below pre-Covid levels on falling new-home prices, rising input costs, weakening construction starts, rising inventory and crashed NAHB buyer sentiment. It adds a long S&P 500 equal-weight (RSP) vs short homebuilders (XHB) trade at a 1.75:1 ratio. Separately, its Taiwan-vs-India and Japan-banks trades were stopped out; it now prefers short JPY rates via long Canada vs short Japan 2y government bonds.
